target.title: fix(macos): prevent hatch and web chat from timing out on slow first replies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where macOS onboarding/web chat could make a slow first assistant reply look stuck or prematurely timed out when the selected model takes longer than the old client-side budget. This matters for first-run hatch/chat paths with slower models such as OpenAI 5.5, where the user expects the assistant to keep working after they describe its purpose.

The mismatch was that the macOS WebChat path needed a longer assistant-run budget and a completion observation path, while the request/ACK deadline should still fail quickly when the gateway is unreachable.

## Why This Change Was Made

This separates the short request/ACK deadline from the actual WebChat assistant run budget. The shared `GatewayConnection.chatSend` default stays request-sized so other macOS callers such as Talk Mode keep their existing timeout policy, while every `MacGatewayChatTransport` send path explicitly opts WebChat/hatch into one shared five-minute `timeoutMs` run budget. This includes normal sends, selected-agent/routing-contract sends, and outbox replay sends.

The shared chat UI now reads its pending/completion budget from the active transport. The default transport budget remains 120 seconds, while macOS WebChat overrides it to five minutes and waits for completion through the existing Gateway `agent.wait` surface before refreshing history. The change does not alter gateway protocol shape, auth, provider routing, model selection, session storage, schema, migrations, or delivery channels.

## User Impact

macOS users hatching or chatting with a newly configured assistant now get a realistic wait window and a production completion observation path for slow first replies instead of a premature timeout or stuck-looking state while the assistant run may still be active or recently completed.

The intended behavior is that macOS WebChat/hatch keeps gateway ACK failures prompt while giving only the WebChat assistant run, UI pending state, and completion refresh path the first-run-sized five-minute window.

## Evidence

- Current conflict-repair head: `f8f78c9ead27845d9f93fb963c8fa9012c2d6fa4`, rebased on `origin/main` `e26a850fbdd6fa5703f9423f5bc2d5dcbc5c8d0c`.
- The latest-main rebase preserved selected-agent/global-session routing and route-capture parameters. A post-rebase review found that the selected-agent and outbox `chat.send` call sites had omitted the five-minute run budget and therefore fell back to 30 seconds. This head fixes all three macOS WebChat send paths by using one shared `300_000` ms run-budget constant.
- The regression test now sends through both the normal and selected-agent transport overloads and asserts that both emitted gateway payloads contain `timeoutMs == 300_000`; it also verifies that the targeted payload carries the selected `agentId`.
- Full-diff review found that terminal `agent.wait` failures could skip history reconciliation and leave the extended pending spinner active. This head now reconciles `error` results and `timeout` snapshots carrying terminal gateway metadata (`endedAt`, timeout phase, stop reason, or equivalent markers), while keeping plain wait-deadline timeouts and pending-error snapshots non-terminal. Focused decoder tests cover each case.
- Current-head local checks:
  ```text
  swiftformat --lint --config config/swiftformat <3 changed Swift files>
  0/3 files require formatting.

  swift test --package-path apps/macos --skip-update --filter 'mac chat transport keeps first-run budget for direct and targeted sends'
  1 test passed.

  swift test --package-path apps/macos --skip-update --filter 'terminal agent wait results reconcile history while wait deadlines stay pending'
  1 test passed.

  swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter 'completion wait'
  3 tests passed.

  swiftlint lint --config config/swiftlint.yml <3 changed Swift files>
  2 pre-existing warnings, 0 serious violations.

  xcrun swiftc -frontend -parse <3 changed Swift files>
  exit 0

  git diff --check
  exit 0
  ```
- The local Swift toolchain limitations were resolved: SwiftFormat was upgraded to the repository-required 0.62.1, and the locked Peekaboo and Sparkle dependencies were hydrated successfully. The exact current head passes SwiftFormat and all five focused macOS/shared Swift tests listed above.
- The prior packaged-app proof was recorded on pre-rebase head `c54a17b39c8314b0788797dff114928ac57dd492`: a prompt sent through the real native `OpenClaw Chat` input remained visibly `Writing` for more than 32 seconds without timing out, then displayed `OPENCLAW_C54A17B39C_SLOW_REPLY_DONE` and cleared the pending indicator. This remains behavior evidence for the same PR direction, but it is not represented as fresh live proof for the current SHA.
- No fresh packaged-app/model-provider run was available in the current local environment. No video recording was produced.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: exact-head focused Swift unit tests plus macOS packaged-app behavior proof from the pre-rebase patch. A fresh packaged-app/model-provider run was not available locally.
- Target test files: `apps/macos/Tests/OpenClawIPCTests/GatewayConnectionControlTests.swift`, `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Tests/OpenClawKitTests/ChatViewModelTests.swift`.
- Scenario locked in: both normal and selected-agent macOS WebChat sends emit `timeoutMs == 300_000`, outbox replay uses the same run-budget constant, completion waits use the transport-scoped budget, terminal success/error results trigger history reconciliation, wait-only timeouts remain non-terminal, pending runs survive past 30 seconds, and pending state clears after completion.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the tests cover the two changed seams directly: macOS transport timeout selection and shared chat pending/completion state.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: the macOS WebChat send path used one short timeout value for both request/ACK delivery and the assistant run budget, so a slow first reply could look timed out or stuck even while the gateway run was still active.
- Missing detection / guardrail: the regression covered only the original non-targeted transport overload, so a conflict-resolution change could add selected-agent and outbox send sites that silently inherited the 30-second default. The updated test covers the selected-agent overload and the implementation centralizes the run budget used by all three send sites.
